propositions: The absolute byte-floor watermark (2 GiB) is crossed only at 93.3% usage on a 30-GiB volume, sitting above the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% incident peak, so the janitor never engages before the alarm fires.

The 7-day cold-trim TTL exceeds the container lifetime (recreated hourly), and the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is not implemented in _gc_pass, leaving the absolute watermark as the only live reclaim trigger.

The snapshot store is on the container writable layer (root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere, so store_root() falls through to tempfile.gettempdir(), making bytes invisible to prune_docker_caches.

Adding a volume-relative headroom term (free_watermark_pct as integer percent) with hysteresis (RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT fixed at 5 points) scales the trigger below the alarm floor on small volumes without breaking the absolute floor on large ones.
The fix defaults free_watermark_pct to 0 (off) so existing deployments are unchanged, and the review-bot service opts in at 20 to reclaim at 80% used, matching autodeploy.sh's DISK_PRESSURE_PCT.

Runtime experiment on a 30-GiB volume with injected free-space values proves 0 evictions at 85% and 90% used under current code, and GREEN with the fix at 82% (below alarm floor) when free_watermark_pct=20.
